Where it began

Shai Hope was born in Barbados on 10 November 1993 and went to secondary school at Queen's College in Saint James. Cricket runs in the family: his elder brother, Kyle, also became a professional cricketer.

Part of his education came in England, at Bedes Senior School in East Sussex, where the former Sussex captain Alan Wells looked after his cricket. He took the school's first eleven to a national T20 final, and in 2012 he played a season of village cricket for Chiddingly. Back home he made 211 for Barbados against the Windward Islands, and in 2017 he scored hundreds in both the semi-final and the final as Barbados won the Regional Super50.

The player

He first played Test cricket against England in May 2015, and his great Test came at Headingley in August 2017. He made 147 in the first innings and 118 not out in the second as West Indies chased 322 to win by five wickets, their first away Test win over England since 2000. Nobody had made two hundreds in a first-class match at Headingley before. The next spring Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year.

By November 2026 he had played 49 Tests, making 2,518 runs at 27.98 with five hundreds, and he had taken 30 catches and made two stumpings with the gloves on.

What made him special

One-day cricket is where he did his most consistent work. He opened with John Campbell in a stand of 365 against Ireland in Dublin in 2019, at the time the highest for the first wicket in any ODI, and in Dublin that May he also made 170 against Ireland, his best one-day score. He became the first cricketer to make international hundreds against every Full Member nation, and he reached 5,000 ODI runs in 114 innings, as quickly as Viv Richards had. In 2023 he took over as West Indies' one-day captain and marked the occasion with 128 not out against South Africa.

Test cricket made him wait. After Headingley his next Test hundred was eight years coming, but when the runs returned they came in a rush: 103 against India, 140 at Christchurch and 112 against Sri Lanka.

Away from the middle

Cricket West Indies made him its Cricketer of the Year in 2018, along with its Test and ODI awards, and he was picked in the ICC's ODI team of the year in 2020 and again in 2022. He has also captained Barbados and turned out briefly for Yorkshire in 2023, making 83 on his debut for the county.

And finally

His 140 at Christchurch in December 2025 helped West Indies to 457 for six in the fourth innings and a draw. No side had made more in the last innings of a Test since England's 654 for six in the famous timeless Test of 1939. England had all the time in the world that day. West Indies did not, which made theirs all the sweeter.
